RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Reese Jennings
Member ID: W714739496
Reference Number: POC-0A9468429E-28212
Date of Notice: 2026-08-16
Requested Service: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-12

To the Grievance and Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551, ordered by my surgeon, Dr. Duval (orthopedic surgery). The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I dispute this determination because the clinical record already in your possession documents an extensive, multi-modal, supervised trial of conservative care that substantially exceeds any duration threshold I have been able to identify in the medical-necessity criteria applicable to this service.

1. Which criteria apply

Anthem's determination letter does not name or quote the specific medical policy or clinical review criteria applied to my case. Based on my own research, Anthem Blue Cross delegates medical-necessity review of spine surgery, including ACDF, to its musculoskeletal-surgery review vendor, Carelon Medical Benefits Management, under Carelon's "Appropriate Use Criteria: Spine Surgery" guideline, section "Cervical Decompression With or Without Fusion." I was able to confirm, from Carelon's own public guideline library, the version of that guideline in effect on the date of this denial (Effective Date 11/15/2025, updated for codes 01/01/2026). I was not able to obtain the complete text of the "Clinical Indications" section for that guideline — only the portions quoted below, which I located and verified in Carelon's publicly posted guideline text. I am therefore not quoting or attributing to Anthem any policy language beyond what is set out below, and I am asking Anthem, as part of this appeal, to provide the complete, current text of the specific criteria it applied to my request, including the document title, Doc ID/version number, and effective date, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it point by point.

The portions of the Carelon guideline I was able to verify state:

"Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirm the diagnosis or establish its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention."

and, in the cervical decompression/fusion section:

"...unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)..."

I am not quoting any other portion of the guideline (for example, any instability- or deformity-specific provisions) because I was not able to independently verify that text, and I do not believe those alternate provisions are the ones at issue in my case in any event, since my case presents as radiculopathy with conservative-care failure, addressed by the quoted language above.

2. How my record satisfies the quoted criteria

- Duration and nature of symptoms: I have had 9 months of progressive neck pain, unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain and numbness radiating into my right thumb and index finger, accompanied by weakness. This is a chronic, progressive, and functionally limiting condition, not an acute or self-limited episode.

- Conservative management far exceeding 6 weeks: I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-04-01 through 2026-06-24, 18 visits), including cervical traction and postural training, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This is twice the minimum duration referenced in the quoted Carelon criterion ("at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management"). In addition, I was treated with NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-16, which produced only 2 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, the record documents a conservative-care trial that is longer, more varied, and more thoroughly supervised than the quoted threshold requires.

- Objective correlation between symptoms and imaging: MRI of the cervical spine on 2026-07-22 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This finding directly corresponds to my clinical presentation (right thumb/index finger radicular pain and numbness, C6 distribution) and to the positive provocative testing and neurologic deficit documented on examination "corresponding to the imaged level." This satisfies the requirement, reflected in the general framework quoted above, that the diagnosis be confirmed through "a complete evaluation of the patient," including "history and physical examination," "diagnostic testing," and documented "response to prior therapeutic intervention" — all of which are present and unfavorable to further conservative care in my chart.

- Absence of contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker. Nothing in my record raises a competing safety concern that would outweigh the anticipated benefit of surgery.

Given (a) 9 months of progressive symptoms, (b) 12 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy with cervical traction and postural training, (c) 6 months of NSAID therapy, (d) a corticosteroid injection with only transient partial relief, and (e) imaging that objectively correlates with my neurologic findings, the record documents a conservative-treatment trial that meets or exceeds the 6-week benchmark quoted above, and documents the "response to prior therapeutic intervention" that the general clinical framework calls for. The stated basis for denial — lack of documentation of an adequate conservative-care trial — is not supported by the record.

3. Relief requested

I ask that Anthem:
1. Reverse the denial and approve CPT 22551 (ACDF) as requested by Dr. Duval; or
2. If Anthem maintains the denial, provide the complete text of the specific medical policy/clinical guideline (title, Doc ID/version, and effective date) and the specific criterion or criteria it contends have not been met, so that my surgeon and I can respond directly; and
3. Confirm the process and timeframe for a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Duval and Anthem's reviewing physician, consistent with the guideline language quoted above contemplating such a conversation when appropriateness is in question.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-24, 18 visits), records of NSAID therapy (6 months) and the 2026-05-16 corticosteroid injection, the 2026-07-22 MRI report, and Dr. Duval's clinical notes documenting exam findings and neurologic deficit.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in your notice (by 2027-02-12). Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and advise of the applicable decision timeframe. If this appeal is denied, please provide the information required to request an Independent Medical Review through the California Department of Managed Health Care.

Sincerely,

Reese Jennings
Member ID: W714739496

Enclosures: [physical therapy discharge note; medication/injection records; 2026-07-22 MRI report; surgeon's clinical notes; Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-16]
